title: State Management Applied Check
description: Practice choosing between local state, context, Redux Toolkit, Zustand, atom stores, server cache, and URL state.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A dropdown open flag is used only inside one menu component. Where should it usually live?
questions.explanation: Very local UI state should stay near the component that owns it.

questions.prompt: A product search page has filters that should be bookmarkable and shareable. What is a good home for them?
questions.explanation: Shareable view state such as filters and sorting often belongs in the URL.

questions.prompt: A shopping cart is used across many routes and updated by several components. Which tools could be reasonable? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Context with reducer for moderate complexity
Redux Toolkit for structured global updates
Zustand for a lightweight external store
A local useState inside one button only

questions.explanation: Shared client state can fit context plus reducer, Redux Toolkit, or Zustand depending on complexity and team needs.

questions.prompt: A list of users comes from an API and needs caching, loading states, errors, and revalidation. What category is it?
questions.explanation: Remote data should be treated as server state with cache and synchronization concerns.

questions.prompt: Reducers should stay pure and avoid starting network requests inside reducer logic.
questions.explanation: Reducers calculate next state from inputs; async work belongs in thunks, effects, or data libraries.

questions.prompt: A Redux slice needs to update state after an async save succeeds. What Redux Toolkit feature can help model the async flow?

options.text: createAsyncThunk or similar async logic outside reducers

questions.explanation: RTK supports async thunks that dispatch lifecycle actions handled by reducers.

questions.prompt: When might atom-based stores like Jotai or Recoil fit? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Many small independent pieces of state
A need to avoid one large centralized object

questions.explanation: Atom stores can model granular client state and derived relationships; they do not replace backend security.

questions.prompt: A team asks which state library to pick. What should guide the decision first?

options.text: State ownership, sharing scope, update complexity, async needs, and team familiarity
Whether it makes state immutable automatically everywhere

questions.explanation: Tool choice should follow the problem: who owns the state, who reads it, how it changes, and what the team can maintain.
